prompt.text:
Implement an ordered document archive in `solution.rs` using only the Rust standard library.

Expose these declarations:

- `pub struct Document { pub id: u64, pub title: String, pub pages: u32 }`
- `pub enum ArchiveError { ZeroId, EmptyTitle, ZeroPages, DuplicateId, NotFound }`
- `pub struct Archive`
- `Document::new(id: u64, title: impl Into<String>, pages: u32) -> Result<Self, ArchiveError>`
- `Archive::new() -> Self`
- `Archive::add(&mut self, document: Document) -> Result<(), ArchiveError>`
- `Archive::remove(&mut self, id: u64) -> Result<Document, ArchiveError>`
- `Archive::get(&self, id: u64) -> Option<&Document>`
- `Archive::documents(&self) -> &[Document]`
- `Archive::total_pages(&self) -> u64`

A document requires a nonzero ID, a title containing at least one non-ASCII-whitespace character, and a nonzero page count. Preserve the title exactly. IDs are unique. Documents remain in insertion order. Removing an existing document returns it and preserves the relative order of all remaining documents. Adding a duplicate or removing a missing ID must not mutate the archive. `total_pages` must avoid narrow integer overflow by summing as `u64` and must not mutate anything. An empty archive is valid. Do not include a `main` function.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.
